# Andrew Byrley

> Andrew Byrley has been a U.S. diplomat since 2010, with assignments in Europe, Africa, and Central America. He trained as a mechanical and robotics engineer, and when he can't find a fix for a problem, he likes building one himself.

This is Andrew Byrley's personal site. Views expressed here are his own and do not represent the U.S. Government.

## Pages

- [Home](https://andrewbyrley.com/): Short bio, projects, and a summary of his work.
- [Resume](https://andrewbyrley.com/resume/): Foreign Service assignments, technology policy work, publications, projects, and education.

## Projects

- [FEHB Survey 2026](https://andrewbyrley.com/fehb/): Anonymous survey of 80 Foreign Service households on their FEHB health plans, published before 2027 Open Season.
- [Global city light analysis](https://github.com/byrleyar/light-analysis): Python tool that uses satellite night-light data to compare economic activity where GDP data is unreliable.
- [Color-changing lamp](https://hackaday.io/project/178435-mr-miffy-rgb-led-module): Battery-powered Zigbee LED module for a children's lamp, controlled from Home Assistant.

## Work

- U.S. Foreign Service, 2010-present: assignments in Riga, Washington, Nouakchott, and Belmopan; started as a Security Engineering Officer with Diplomatic Security.
- French Center for AI Safety (CeSIA), Brussels, 2026: Senior EU Engagement Officer.
- Centre for the Governance of AI (GovAI), London, 2026: Winter Fellow.
- [From TCP/IP to MCP: Security and Governance Lessons from Internet Protocols for Agentic AI](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26624) (2026), with Ben Bucknall and Lewis Hammond.
